//: Coverage scope is the query/schema/error runtime. Excludes: tooling (cli/, generate.ts, introspect.ts), edge shim (serverless.ts, tested via pg-compat contract), package barrel (index.ts), and test helpers. Codegen is covered by end-to-end tests in test/cli.test.ts and test/generate-relations.test.ts; raising line coverage on it would require mocking filesystem + child_process in unit tests without adding real signal.
//cli-gate: The `src/cli/**` exclusion above is NOT the whole story since 2026-07-28. Three CLI files are the highest-consequence code in the package: cli/studio.ts has a WRITE MODE that executes mutations and a PII redaction path, cli/migrate.ts runs destructive DDL, and cli/destructive.ts is the scanner that decides what counts as destructive. They were unmeasured, which hid the fact that they are ALREADY well tested (studio-write.test.ts is 1,546 lines, studio-demo.test.ts 973, migrate.test.ts 771) and, worse, left no ratchet on them: coverage could fall to zero without any gate noticing. They now have their OWN gate, `npm run test:coverage:cli`, run as its own CI job. It is a SEPARATE c8 invocation rather than an entry in the `include` list here because c8 checks one threshold set per run: folding these files into this run would let a studio.ts regression hide behind the query runtime's numbers, which is the same masking the blanket exclusion produced. cli/index.ts stays out of both gates: it is 4,759 lines of argument parsing and command dispatch whose behavior is asserted through the CLI end-to-end tests, and its uncovered `process.exit` paths would dominate any floor set over it.
//cli-gate-per-file: The CLI gate is PER FILE, not aggregate-only, since 2026-07-28. An aggregate floor lets the least-covered file spend the slack the best-covered file earned, which is the same masking the blanket `src/cli/**` exclusion produced, one level down: measured on 0.61.0 the three files hold 2960/3662 lines (80.83%), an 80% floor needs 2930, so there were 30 covered lines of slack, ALL of which migrate.ts could spend by falling from 70.27% to 68.18% with the aggregate still green. c8 cannot express three different floors in one invocation (`--per-file` applies the SAME numbers to every file), so `npm run test:coverage:cli` is now one collection run plus four `c8 report --check-coverage` passes over the coverage already on disk, three per-file and one aggregate. Re-reporting costs no extra test run. The aggregate pass is KEPT, it is the only thing that catches all three files sagging together inside their individual margins. A gate run with no collected coverage exits 1 (ENOENT on coverage/tmp) rather than reporting a vacuous pass, which is checked.
//cli-gate-measurements: MEASURED 2026-07-28 on 0.61.0, no database, by `npm run coverage:cli:collect`. THESE ARE THE FIGURES `--check-coverage` COMPARES AGAINST, read from the json-summary reporter, NOT the text table's columns. That distinction is load-bearing and cost a round to find: c8's text reporter prints a `% Lines` column derived from statements, so it showed studio.ts at 86.31 and the aggregate at 81.45 while check-coverage was comparing 84.97 and 80.83 against the same floors. The 2026-07-28 round-1 note set the floors from the text table, so the aggregate lines margin it recorded as 1.45 was really 0.62. Gate figures: aggregate lines/statements 80.62, branches 85.83, functions 83.69. Per file: destructive.ts 100 / 100 / 86.72 / 100 (lines / statements / branches / functions); migrate.ts 70.27 / 70.27 / 93.05 / 74.35; studio.ts 84.51 / 84.51 / 83.43 / 88.37. Floors sit ~1.5-2.5 points under, the same margin rule the runtime thresholds use below: destructive 98/98/84/98, studio 82/82/81/86, migrate 68/68/91/72, aggregate 78/78/84/82. The aggregate lines/statements floor was LOWERED from 80 to 78, reason recorded per the rule below: 80 was never the ~1.5 point margin it was documented to be (real margin 0.62), and the per-file passes are now the primary gate while the aggregate is a backstop. CAVEAT on studio.ts: it was being edited concurrently while these were measured and read 86.31, then 84.97, then 84.51 within one session, so its figures are a LOWER BOUND from the last reading, not a settled measurement. Re-measure and ratchet at release time. RULE, unchanged: raise these as coverage improves; never lower one without recording the reason here. The obvious next target is migrate.ts, the least-covered of the three and the one that runs destructive DDL.
//cli-gate-file-list: The gate drives a TARGETED test-file list rather than the whole suite. Round 1 recorded that the whole suite 'produced identical aggregates'; it does not, and the difference is small but real, so it is written down rather than rounded away. MEASURED 2026-07-28, same c8 include/exclude, no database: targeted gives aggregate 81.45 statements / 85.94 branches / 84.61 functions with studio.ts 86.31 (text-reporter columns, compared like for like); the whole suite gives 81.50 / 86.36 / 84.61 with studio.ts 86.42, i.e. 2 extra covered lines in studio.ts from incidental loads elsewhere in the suite. The targeted list is still the right choice, on time rather than on numbers: ~2s wall clock against ~26s for the whole suite under coverage. The round-1 note's '~80s' for the whole-suite figure was wrong, it is the `--test-concurrency=1` runtime-coverage lane, a different command; the plain unit lane's own test duration is ~19s. Because the list is targeted, a new studio/migrate/destructive test file must be ADDED to `coverage:cli:collect` in package.json or its coverage does not count here.
//types-only: query/types.ts, query/deferred.ts and engine-config.ts are type declarations that emit no runtime code (each compiles to `export {};`). c8 counts them only because `all: true` walks every .ts file, so they contributed ~1,600 permanently-uncovered statements of pure denominator noise. Excluding them measures the runtime, not the type surface. engine-config.ts joined this list 2026-07-28: it is 68 lines exporting one type alias, and it alone was holding the lines/statements figure at 74.89, i.e. BELOW its own 75 floor, so the gate was failing on pure denominator noise. This is the sanctioned exclusion above applied to a file that qualified for it, not a threshold being moved to fit a number.
//thresholds: Re-baselined 2026-07-24 to MEASURED values, replacing aspirational numbers that were never met. The old gate (lines/statements 80, functions 82, branches 82) had been failing continuously against a real ~77/61/86, which is how a red gate got normalized and releases shipped over it. A permanently-red gate blocks nothing and teaches everyone to ignore it; a measured floor that can only ratchet upward is worth more. RULE: raise these as coverage improves; never lower one without recording the reason here. TARGET: function coverage back to 70 by 2026-10-01; the 59 floor is a floor, not the goal. The real gap is function coverage in query/builder.ts, query/relations.ts and query/where.ts, tracked as follow-up work, not waived.
//measurements: WITH a seeded Postgres, `npm run test:coverage` (= `c8 tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 src/test/*.test.ts`, the exact command the CI coverage job runs), 2026-07-24: statements 76.98, branches 86.25, functions 60.63, lines 76.98. WITHOUT a database, same command, 2026-07-25: statements 74.85, branches 86.09, functions 59.74, lines 74.85 (450 of 3,293 tests skip behind skipGate). Read those two rows together: a no-database run is a strict LOWER BOUND on the with-database run, because `all: true` fixes the denominator and running the DB-gated tests can only add covered lines. Any reading that shows no-DB ABOVE with-DB is a measurement artifact (different HEAD, different file set), not a real regression in the with-DB number. Thresholds are left where the 2026-07-24 baseline put them: the current no-DB lower bound already clears branches (86.09 vs 85) and functions (59.74 vs 59), and the with-DB run clears lines/statements (76.98 vs 75). They are deliberately NOT ratcheted to the 2026-07-25 reading: the margin over it is 0.09-0.74 points, which is noise, and a floor that tight is a tripwire that gets reflexively re-baselined rather than a gate that means something. Ratchet when a measurement lands with at least ~1 point of real margin, and record the new measurement here. WITH a seeded Postgres, 2026-07-28 on 0.61.0, after excluding engine-config.ts and adding the review regression tests: statements 75.18, branches 87.50, functions 59.83, lines 75.18. Margin over the lines floor is still only 0.18 points, so this is NOT a ratchet point; the honest reading is that the SQL-generating modules (relations.ts 40.7, builder.ts 42.9, where.ts 48.7 lines) are what is holding the whole figure down.
